column1: # ADR registry for the Phase-0 bake-off (the benchmark configuration step 5, plan row
# A24). One row per ADR number that collects variant families.
# The family -> ADR map itself is NOT here: it lives in `ADR=` in each
# hack/bakeoff/<family>.env, next to that family's package, benchmark root and
# reference kind, so one family is described in one place. This file holds
# what belongs to the ADR rather than to a family -- its number, its file name
# and its title -- because an ADR that collects nine families cannot take its
# title from any one of them. Nine env files used to carry the same ADR title,
# and they had already drifted apart from each other.
# `bakeoff adr` renders one file per row below from the per-family scorecards
# in benchmarks/reports/scorecards/. For a number that already has a file in
# adr/, that file's own name and title heading win and the data is attached to
# it inside a delimited generated section; the slug and title columns then
# record what a fresh render would have used.
# extra-variants ("-" when none) are §9 rows the ADR owns that have no env
# file of their own, so `bakeoff adr` still lists them in `variants:`.

column4: Concrete handles implementing narrow interfaces; optional interfaces for SPI growth
Received-message shape and settlement representation (B1, B2)
API surface shapes: key type, headers, options, codec interface, receive iteration, lifecycle and construction (B3-B5, B8, B9, B11, B12)
Capability model: categorical levels with a documented rank, scopes, Limit[T], RequireAtLeast and RequireAny
Safe-copy publication and safe receive are the defaults; reuse, owned and zero-copy are opt-in
Failure policy: dead-letter when an explicit DLQ exists, otherwise halt; error construction and matching
Driver variant decisions: the §9 rows that need a broker and are decided in Part B (A11-A13, A15-A17, A32-A35)
Memory engine internals: lane queue, fan-out storage, wait strategy, timer, hash, pooling, admission, registry and retry lane (A1-A7, A27, A28)
Assumptions ledger and secondary internals (A8, A9, A22, A23, A25, A26, A30)
Encoding and timing internals: wire layout, identifier generator, JSON codec and backoff jitter (A18-A21)
Batch SPI contract, publisher routing and unsafe ring addressing (A36, A37, A10)
